title: A Delivery, Not a Route: A Mission State Machine With a Battery Check, a Timeout for a Blocked Road, and a Pause That Does Not Start Over

questions.question: Why must the battery cover the round trip and a reserve before the mission starts?
options: The reserve is a charge made by the fleet's owner
A full battery keeps the motors warm
Because the check is cheapest to write there
A robot that cannot get home has made a delivery and then become a hazard on the road
questions.explanation: The cheapest place to find out is before it leaves. A robot that runs out on the way back blocks the road with nobody near. Refusing at the start costs one delivery and nothing else.

questions.question: At 0.12 Wh/m used against 0.1 expected, what did checking on the way do?
options: Saved a robot that would have been stranded
Nothing: both robots delivered
Turned back a delivery that would have made it
Stranded the robot 26.7 m out
questions.explanation: 3.07 Wh left, not delivered, where the unchecking robot delivered with 1.98 left. The check uses the rate the robot expects, 0.1, and is cautious. At 0.12 the other robot got home with 1.98 Wh, so this caution cost a delivery.

questions.question: At 0.15 Wh/m, what did the robot that checked only at the start do?
options: Refused to start
Turned back before the drop
Delivered and got home with 0.79 Wh
Delivered and was stranded 26.7 m from home, unable to come back, where the checking robot got home with 0.79 Wh
questions.explanation: It had no way to notice it was using more than planned. The one that checked gave up the delivery and came home.

questions.question: A road is blocked both ways. What state does the mission end in, and why not wait?
options: aborted, back at home with the load
needs help: stopped where it is
done, after waiting for the road to clear
to home, by another route
questions.explanation: There is no safe place to go and waiting for ever or doing something clever are both worse. With the road blocked ahead and behind there is nowhere to go. The mission ends in a state of its own, so that a person is called.

questions.question: The link was lost for 30 s. What did the pause cost?
options: 31.0 s of time, the whole difference (435 s against 404 s), and no energy
A restart from the beginning of the road
The delivery, which was aborted
31.0 s of time and 3 Wh of energy
questions.explanation: The state, position and timers were kept. The mission holds while the supervisor has the robot stopped. Nothing times out, and it carries on from where it was.

questions.question: A margin of 1.5 on the rate stranded none in 72 worlds. What did it cost?
options: Nothing: it only removed the stranded ones
54 of 72 missions refused and half as many delivered
A larger battery in every robot
5 more stranded robots
questions.explanation: Safety bought with work, for the owner to choose. Planning for half as much energy again strands nobody and turns down most of the work. Which to prefer is the fleet owner's choice.
